title: Circle theorems
examples: What is the relationship between the angle at the centre and the angle at the circumference?
Can you show me how to prove the angle in a semicircle is a right angle?
If two chords intersect inside a circle, how do I find the angle formed?

explain.say: Today we learn some important circle theorems. These help us find angles inside a circle. We will learn how to prove these rules.
First, we look at the angle at the centre. The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the same arc. This is a key rule to remember.

draw.text: Angle at Centre = 2 x Angle at Circumference

explain.say: Next, consider the angle in a semicircle. This angle is always a right angle, which means ninety degrees. This is a very useful theorem.
Another rule is angles subtended by the same arc. These angles are equal to each other. They are always the same size.

draw.text: Angles in same segment are equal

explain.say: Now, let's look at intersecting chords. The angle formed is double the sum of the intercepted arcs. This is for angles inside the circle.

faq.q: What is the angle at the centre theorem really about?
faq.a: It states that the angle formed at the centre of the circle is exactly double the angle formed at the edge on the same arc. This comes from the definition of the arc.
asks: How do I use the centre angle rule?
Is the centre angle always twice the other angle?

faq.q: Does the angle in a semicircle always mean ninety degrees?
faq.a: Yes, if the angle is formed by the diameter, it must be ninety degrees. This is a direct consequence of the angle in a semicircle theorem.
asks: What is the right angle rule for a circle?
If I use the diameter, what angle do I get?

faq.q: If two angles are in the same segment, are they always equal?
faq.a: Yes, any two angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal. They share the same intercepted arc.
asks: Do I need to prove angles in the same segment?
Are angles on the same side of the arc equal?

faq.q: What if the chords intersect outside the circle?
faq.a: That is a different theorem. For intersecting chords outside the circle, the angle is half the difference of the intercepted arcs.
asks: What about angles formed outside the circle?
How do I find the angle if the lines cross outside?

faq.q: Can I use these theorems if the circle is not drawn perfectly?
faq.a: The theorems rely on the points lying on the circle's circumference. You must assume the points are on the circle for the theorems to apply.
asks: Do the points have to be on the circle?
What if the points are inside the circle?

facts: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
The angle in a semicircle is always ninety degrees.
Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal.
The angle formed by two intersecting chords inside is half the sum of the intercepted arcs.

quiz.say: If an angle at the centre is ninety degrees, what is the angle at the circumference on the same arc?
quiz.why: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. So, ninety degrees divided by two is forty-five degrees.

wrong.0: This forgets to divide the centre angle by two.
wrong.1: This confuses the angle with the full circle measurement.
wrong.3: This incorrectly divides the angle by four instead of two.

quiz.say: A triangle inscribed in a circle has one side as the diameter. What is the angle opposite the diameter?

options.show: the same as the centre angle
options.say: the same as the centre angle

quiz.why: The angle opposite the diameter always forms a right angle, which is ninety degrees by theorem.

wrong.0: This confuses the angle with the sum of angles in a triangle.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes the angle is half of ninety degrees.
wrong.3: This mixes up the rule for the centre angle with the semicircle rule.

quiz.say: Two angles are formed by the same arc. If one angle is thirty degrees, what is the other angle?
quiz.why: Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are always equal to each other.

wrong.0: This suggests the angles cancel each other out.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds the angles together.
wrong.3: This incorrectly calculates half of the given angle.
